correctness_confidence.basis: Verified 18 constructive Lean 4 theorems with zero axioms, zero sorry, and zero warnings in ConnectivitySwitching.lean, alongside 16 canonical exact-Z certificates replayed deterministically with zero floating-point arithmetic.

novelty.basis: Pioneers machine-checked exact-integer formalizations and zero-float certificate auditing for graph connectivity switching, matroid intersection duality, and parameterized WSAT reductions.

reproducibility.basis: All 16 canonical certificates, Lean 4 proofs, and Python verifier scripts are fully specified, deterministic, and verified end-to-end via scripts/verify_all.py with SHA-256 integrity hashes.

rigor.basis: Exhaustive 41-graph 4-vertex dichotomy census, 224-assignment NNF truth-table sweeps, and 57/57 adversarial red-team forgery rejections demonstrate exceptional methodological rigor and formal precision.

significance.basis: Establishes a rigorous, manifest-locked certificate architecture for complex graph switching and reconfiguration problems, bridging theoretical complexity theory with mechanized proof verification.

strengths: Zero-dependency, zero-sorry Lean 4 formalization of 18 core combinatorial and reduction theorems.
Pure Python zero-floating-point certificate auditor with strict JSON AST typing across four distinct modes.
Comprehensive empirical evaluation including exhaustive 41-graph census, 224-assignment WSAT sweeps, and 57/57 adversarial forgery rejections.
strong_novelty_candidates: Machine-checked exact-integer certificate architecture for graph connectivity switching and matroid intersection.
summary: This paper presents a machine-checked exact-integer formalization and zero-float certificate auditor (SWITCH-GRAPH-CONN-CERT-1.0) for connectivity switching in graphs, covering complete-multipartite dichotomy, Edmonds matroid-intersection duality, shifted-weight telescoping, and series-parallel WSAT reductions via an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel and 16 canonical certificates.
weaknesses: Scope explicitly excludes formalization of asymptotic runtime bounds and complexity-class separation reductions (NP/W[1]/W[SAT]/ETH) in Lean 4.
